source.title: Muon Is Theoretically Wrong For Convolutions, But Empirically Effective
source.authors: Thibaut Boissin; Thomas Massena; Mathieu Serrurier; F. Mamalet

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some equations, tables, and figures are garbled in the supplied extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizers on natural image classification and reports training and validation accuracy, but does not test any listed version’s specific intervention or comparison.
record.gate_note: The paper reports train and validation accuracy for Muon variants and SGD; these results bear on generalization performance but do not test the listed versions. Cited optimizer and generalization findings are not treated as results.
record.test_reason: The study tests convolutional update geometry and early optimization efficiency, not any listed claim version. Muon-versus-SGD accuracy comparisons do not test V4's comparison of adaptive gradient methods with SGD. Wilson et al. is cited, but its finding is neither tested nor used as a tool. Update orthogonality is not V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors find that reshape-based Muon generally fails to orthogonalize the convolution operator, while Conv-NS improves operator orthogonality with comparable classification performance. Additional iterations can degrade optimization. They suggest that exact convolutional orthogonality may overconstrain updates and argue that the convolutional polar factor need not solve the full operator-norm LMO; overconstraint as the empirical cause remains a hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: Compares convolutional-aware Muon variants and SGD on natural image classification; it does not use the random-label memorization protocol or test the interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, epoch budget, optimizer, and Conv-NS iteration count affect reported accuracy; batch sizes also differ across dataset and budget settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Under short training budgets, both Muon variants outperform the reported SGD baseline in held-out accuracy. Conv-NS and reshape-based Muon achieve similar accuracy: 93.98 versus 94.02 on eight-epoch CIFAR-10 and 74.53 versus 74.82 on thirty-epoch ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These Muon recipes improve early image-classification performance relative to the reported SGD recipes; convolution-aware orthogonalization gives performance comparable to reshape-based Muon.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 and Tables 2 and 6 show that increasing Conv-NS iterations beyond ten can worsen both training and validation performance despite improving update orthogonality.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More accurate convolutional update orthogonalization can hinder early optimization; update orthogonality alone does not predict classification performance.

record.problems: The main CIFAR-10 table reports means with uncertainty, while ImageNet table entries have no uncertainty estimates. Validation accuracy is not explicitly identified as test accuracy. Training budgets are short, and the authors state performance becomes increasingly capped by network capacity as training gets longer.
record.rows_left_out: None. All reported train and validation accuracy entries in Table 1 are recorded separately. Other comparisons in the text and appendices concern orthogonality, runtime, or cited prior results rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting or natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate training data.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected architecture comparison or learned-locality intervention.

No adaptive-gradient-versus-SGD comparison. Adam is used in auxiliary numerical optimization and parameter groups, not as a controlled classifier-level comparator. No relevant tuning, switching, or decoupled-weight-decay ablation.
No controlled batch-size comparison at a fixed epoch budget; batch size and epoch budget change together.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, gap-ranking analysis, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of examples selected by label memorization and comparison with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 values and stated model, epoch, and batch-size conditions match the supplied text. These rows belong under fits_no_version rather than claim evidence. The record's statements that paired gaps are unavailable are too strong: paired accuracies are provided, although the text does not establish that training and validation metrics use comparable evaluation conditions. E4 incorrectly links the iteration sweep to R7–R10, which instead record Table 1 optimizer comparisons. No omitted result tests V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fit random labels or compare natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No fully connected image classifier comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers such as Adam with SGD or assess the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Does not compare large and small batches under a fixed epoch budget; batch size differs across dataset and budget settings.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare gap-prediction measures.
